transcript.statement: The performance efficiency of the RollCall system is crucial to ensure timely attendance processing. EFF-01 guarantees real-time updates within 2 seconds, EFF-02 ensures support for 500 concurrent users, and EFF-03 mandates rapid report generation. EFF-04 aligns with SafetyAgent's SAF-04, but focuses on optimized storage. EFF-05 emphasizes responsive access for students, while EFF-06 improves resource utilization, and EFF-07 enhances user experience. Together, these requirements optimize system performance without compromising safety or other quality dimensions.

transcript.statement: Sustainability is critical for the RollCall system to minimize energy consumption and carbon footprint. GRN-01 focuses on energy-efficient algorithms, GRN-02 ensures the use of eco-friendly cloud storage, GRN-03 promotes low-energy communication protocols for real-time updates, and GRN-04 provides report formats that reduce digital resource usage. GRN-05 educates users about their carbon footprint, while GRN-06 aligns data retention policies with sustainable practices. GRN-07 optimizes the user interface for low-power devices, ensuring overall energy efficiency. These requirements should be prioritized to ensure a sustainable system.

conflicts_raised.description: Load balancing in EFF-06 may increase energy consumption, which conflicts with GRN-01's focus on minimizing energy use.

transcript.statement: The Safety & Reliability of the RollCall system is paramount to protect sensitive student attendance data. SAF-01 ensures secure authentication, preventing unauthorized access. SAF-02 guarantees real-time data synchronization to maintain accurate records, while SAF-03 implements automated alerts for discrepancies, enhancing data accuracy. SAF-04's requirement for historical data retention supports long-term analysis and compliance. SAF-05 provides accountability through logging attendance modifications. SAF-06 allows manual overrides in case of failures, ensuring fault tolerance. SAF-07 emphasizes regular security audits to identify vulnerabilities, which is critical for maintaining system integrity. All these requirements are essential for a reliable system that prioritizes safety.

conflicts_raised.description: Both EFF-04 and SAF-04 require historical data retention for 5 years, which may compete for storage resources.

transcript.statement: The Trustworthiness of the RollCall system is essential to ensure data protection and user privacy. TRU-01 mandates encryption for all student attendance data, both at rest and in transit, safeguarding sensitive information. TRU-02 implements role-based access control to limit data access, enhancing security. TRU-03 ensures an audit log for all access and modifications, promoting accountability. TRU-04 requires successful authentication for students to view their records, reinforcing data security. TRU-05 verifies data integrity through checksums or hashes, while TRU-06 allows users to report unauthorized access. TRU-07 enforces session timeouts to protect inactive user sessions. Together, these requirements create a robust framework for security and privacy.

conflicts_raised.description: Both SAF-01 and TRU-01 emphasize the need for secure authentication and data encryption, potentially duplicating efforts.
Manual overrides in SAF-06 could conflict with TRU-02's role-based access control by allowing unauthorized access to sensitive data.
SAF-05's logging mechanism overlaps with TRU-03's audit log, leading to redundancy in logging attendance modifications.

transcript.statement: The ethical and compliance aspects of the RollCall system are crucial to protect student rights and ensure accountability. RES-01 ensures compliance with data protection regulations like GDPR, which is essential for handling sensitive attendance data. RES-02 promotes transparency in attendance recording, fostering trust. RES-03 allows students to dispute records, ensuring fairness. RES-04 mandates anonymized data in reports for privacy protection. RES-05 provides timely notifications to students about their attendance, reinforcing responsibility. RES-06 implements access control for authorized data access, and RES-07 ensures compliance with historical data retention regulations. These requirements collectively uphold ethical standards and legal compliance.

conflicts_raised.description: Both RES-01 and TRU-01 emphasize data protection and encryption, potentially duplicating efforts related to compliance and security.
RES-04's requirement for anonymized attendance reports may overlap with TRU-03's audit logs, creating redundancy in data handling.
Role-based access control in TRU-02 may conflict with RES-06, which also seeks to restrict access but may have different criteria.

requirements.text: The system shall ensure secure authentication and encryption for all user data to prevent unauthorized access and ensure data integrity.
The system shall provide real-time data synchronization to maintain accurate attendance records across multiple classes with a response time of under 2 seconds.
The system shall implement automated alerts for discrepancies in attendance reporting to ensure data accuracy and accountability.
The system shall retain historical attendance data for a minimum of five academic years while ensuring compliance with data protection regulations.
The system shall provide a logging mechanism for all attendance modifications and access attempts to support accountability and traceability.
The system shall allow for manual overrides by authorized personnel in cases of system failure while maintaining strict access controls.
The system shall undergo regular security audits to identify and mitigate potential vulnerabilities.
The system shall ensure attendance data is processed in real-time and generate attendance reports within 5 seconds for up to 1000 students.
The system shall allow students to view their attendance records with a response time of under 3 seconds.
The system shall incorporate energy-efficient load balancing strategies to optimize resource utilization without compromising performance.
The system shall implement low-energy communication protocols for real-time attendance updates to minimize energy consumption.
The system shall provide transparency in attendance recording by logging all attendance changes with timestamps and user identification.
The system shall include mechanisms for students to dispute attendance records through a formal process within 10 days of marking.
The system shall implement role-based access control to restrict data access based on user roles while ensuring compliance with data protection regulations.
